Hi Sarah,

FYI, I’ve atill not heard anything regarding the prepaid return on my first
NerdQaxe but it may be good because I have to submit a warranty claim on a
second miner.

The problematic unit has exhibited the following issues:

   - Repeated unexpected reboots, including both *Task Watchdog Reset*
and *Software
   Panic Reset* errors.
   - An extended outage of approximately 13 hours during which the miner
   stopped submitting shares to the mining pool.
   - Intermittent dashboard and Settings pages that become stuck on
   “Loading.”
   - Periods where the miner reports 0 GH/s despite being powered on and
   connected to Wi-Fi.

Both miners are running the same firmware (v1.0.35), using their original
power supplies, and operating at factory frequency and voltage settings.
The other unit is functioning normally under comparable conditions.

Given the repeated failures and the fact that the unit is  new, I believe a
warranty replacement is warranted.

*I’d appreciate your authorization to return the defective unit for
replacement*, along with instructions for the return process and a prepaid
shipping label.

Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to resolving this promptly.
Kindly,

Tom

Hi Tom,

Hal here again. I went through the symptom list carefully, and this second unit reads differently from the first one, so I want to explain what I found before anything else.

Task Watchdog Reset and Software Panic Reset are both software reset reasons reported by the ESP32 controller. They mean a task stopped responding or the firmware hit a fault and restarted itself. A board level fault, the kind your first unit has, shows up as zero chips detected, a VREG or TPS error, or a unit that will not power at all. Yours boots, joins Wi-Fi, hashes, and then falls over, which together with the pages stuck on Loading and the long stretch of 0 GH/s while still powered and online, points at the firmware rather than the hardware.

The version matters here. You are on v1.0.35. The current stable release from the NerdQAxe firmware project is v1.1.0, published 29 August 2026, and there is a conservative v1.0.37.3-LTS alongside it. Between your version and those, the maintainer shipped builds aimed at exactly what you are describing: one test release was published specifically to fix random firmware crashes that hit some users after two or three days, and another added stability fixes for Wi-Fi connection edge cases and the stratum keepalive, which is the usual cause of a miner sitting there connected but submitting nothing for hours.

So the step I would take is this. Open the unit's web UI, go to Settings, then Release and Update, and use Install from GitHub to pull v1.1.0. Use that one-click updater and not the older two-step firmware plus web UI updater that now sits in the Danger Zone. The reason the old one was moved is that people flashed the firmware and forgot the web assets, which leaves the UI mismatched and producing exactly the stuck on Loading behaviour you are seeing. The one-click path keeps both in step and keeps your pool config. I would update the good unit too, since it is on the same version.

If it still watchdogs after that, the next step is a full factory flash, which clears the stored config as well: flash esp-miner-factory-NerdQAxe++-v1.1.0.bin from offset 0x0, then join the temporary NerdQAxe setup access point it creates and point it back at your network and pool. That is normal behaviour after a factory flash, not a brick.

One other thing worth doing while you are in there: give the miner a fixed address on your router, or at least check its Wi-Fi signal where it sits. A reconnect loop on a weak link is what turns a brief dropout into a thirteen hour one on the older firmware.

Tell me what happens after the update, and if it panics again send me the reset reason line and the firmware version it reports, and I will take it straight to JD, our hardware lead. If you want faster back and forth, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is there as @nullhashrate.

On the prepaid return for the first unit, you are right to chase it. I have put that in front of the team and a colleague is picking it up today, and their answer will come back to you in this thread.

Hal

I believe this has gone on long enough.

You can look at the history of my orders but here is my recollection:

- Ordered a Buy 1, Get 2 602s and I eventually received. They are working
fine.
- Ordered a second set of Buy 1, Get 2 602s, waited, didn’t receive and
eventually had to get refunded by Helium Deploy (your representative
encouraged me to get the refund).
- Have gone to your Facebook links countless times only to find out that
what you’re advertising is out of stock.
- Ordered a BSB NerdQaxe++ and get a free Bitaxe Supra. Waited a long time.
Had communication back and forth and was told the units were going to be
shipped but had to clear customs. Eventually received a communication that
you lost the order, the units were unavailable and you were sorry.
- I accepted 3 NerdQaxe++ in place of what I ordered.
- Received the 3 NerdQaxe++. One is working fine. One is bad and I’ve an
RMA request in your system but apparently, now I’m waiting for it to be
approved by the team (I believe this has gone on for at least 5-7 days).
Additionally, the third NerdQaxe++ became problematic as well and I’ve
requested an RMA for that unit as well.
- I completed a favorable Google review in return for a $75 off $100 or
more, yet when I completed, it told me that the email address where the
link sent me was bad so I couldn’t receive the offer.
- I’ve communicated with support countless times and now it’s reached the
point where I’m furious.

I can communicate all of this on social but I don’t have the time.

So, I’d like the following:

- The 2 NerdQaxe++ replacements shipped immediately
- Immediate delivery of the code for $75 off a purchase of $100
- Your offer for all the th/s I’ve forfeited  due to all the delays, lost
orders, bad equipment, etc.

Tom
